name: Sticker / maximalist / bold-outline explainer
look: thick-outline stickers, flat icons, chart popups on one giant canvas with a camera.

type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: heavy rounded (Rubik, Gilroy Black); candy palette + black outlines.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour is the candy colour of the hero stickers
brand_lock.type_role: heavy rounded display; brand face for the claim
brand_lock.world_changes: sticker slaps, a giant canvas with a camera, doodle arrows
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects_note: No shader finish needed; the style is carried by layout, type and motion.

codex_assets.prompt_template: sticker set of {subject}: cut-outs with thick white border, flat icons, candy palette, laid out on an equal grid on a flat pure chroma-green (#00FF00) background, one sticker per cell, no text
codex_assets.r1_note: sticker sets (cut-outs with white borders), icon packs; A1 + overshoot springs.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: Sticker pack
palettes.words: cream-yellow, ink black, hot pink, royal blue, mint, orange

palettes.name: Cotton candy
palettes.words: pale pink, deep purple ink, violet, mint

brand_lock.rule: Brand colour is the largest sticker and the title fill; other stickers pick from the style palette; the outline ink and the white sticker border stay style-fixed. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Heavy rounded sans with a 0.1em black outline and a 6 px offset shadow; a rotation of -4 to 6 degrees.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...). No shader pass: this style is clean by design; adding a pass is a mistake.

composition.grid: dense collage of white-bordered stickers with a 3 px black outline, overlapping, rotated; one big sticker leads
composition.product_ui: UI is its own sticker (rounded rect with a white border) with the real capture inside

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: flat graphic plate; stickers are 2D vectors, optional 3 degrees of peel curl. Lighting: none, flat; a tiny highlight corner on the peel. Material: die-cut vinyl stickers with a 6 px white border, 3 px black outline and flat fills. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: none; clean vector. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no photoreal, no gradients, no thin lines, no sad palettes, no readable tiny text, no soft shadows.
codex.camera: flat graphic plate; stickers are 2D vectors, optional 3 degrees of peel curl
codex.lighting: none, flat; a tiny highlight corner on the peel
codex.material: die-cut vinyl stickers with a 6 px white border, 3 px black outline and flat fills
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: die-cut vinyl stickers with a 6 px white border; flat graphic plate; stickers are 2D vectors; cream-yellow, ink black, hot pink, royal blue, mint, orange.

sprite_sheet.rules: Not a sprite style. For a cut-out object or character use --transparent (flat #00FF00 key, then despill); one subject, no shadow plane.
